laat_vaar.voor: Gister kon dit reën, en vandag
laat_vaar.na: Dit kan gister gereën het, en vandag
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Gister kon dit reën' reads as 'yesterday it was able to rain'; 'kan ... gereën het' is the natural Afrikaans for a past possibility and keeps the hypothetical meaning.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Gister kon dit reën' is natural Afrikaans for an illustrative possibility parallel to 'vandag kan'; 'Dit kan gister gereën het' turns it into doubt about whether it rained, which moves the meaning and alters the hedge.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Een plek' stresses the number one where nothing is being counted; the indefinite article reads more naturally and keeps the meaning.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Een plek se weer' reads acceptably and stresses one and the same place over many years, matching the 'Een dag' contrast in the next block, so the swap to 'n is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: die weer hoort by jou dorp en die klimaat by die hele wêreld
laat_vaar_vorige.na: dat die weer by jou dorp hoort en die klimaat by die hele wêreld
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: After 'om te dink' a dat-clause with the verb at the end reads more correctly in written Afrikaans; the protected opening stays intact.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Leaving out 'dat' after 'dink' is normal Afrikaans and the original reads well, so adding 'dat' and moving the verb to the end is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'tydperk' is the natural word for a stretch of time that has a length.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'die lengte van die tyd' reads acceptably and matches the heading 'Die verskil is die tyd' and the next sentence's ''n kort tyd', so 'tydperk' is only a different word and breaks that echo.
